Subject: Promo eligibility & packaging question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking a look — quick intro: I run partnerships at BridgeFunding Labs, an early-stage accelerator (cohort-based, ~20 startups running LLM-heavy pilots). We were referred to Redwood by one of our mentors. A couple of questions on packaging and whether promotional credits can be combined with a reserved/dedicated conversion later.

High-level ask: Some of our cohort companies want to use Redwood but are on limited budgets. We typically offer them a combination of (a) your public startup promo credits and (b) an accelerator top-up we manage. Two specific asks:
- Can promo credits be converted or credited against a reserved capacity commitment if the startup decides to upgrade in 60–90 days?
- Is there an exception path to get a larger one-time promo for accredited accelerators (we usually ask for an intake/usage projection & SOW)?

Attached is a quick usage_projection.xlsx and a draft SOW. Timing is tight — cohort kickoff is Oct 20. If there’s a short way to get clarity (and any paperwork we should prepare), let me know.

Appreciate it —
Ethan
Partnerships, BridgeFunding Labs
ethan@bridgefunding.co

Attachments: usage_projection.xlsx (xlsx stub), BridgeFunding_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf stub)

Hi Ethan — thanks for the context and for sharing the projection + SOW. Quick answers up front: we can often support an accelerator top-up and have a limited exception path to allow promo credits to be applied toward an initial reserved conversion, but it’s conditional (and requires finance/legal approval). I’ve looped Ben (Sales Ops) and Laura (Finance) to scope feasibility and the preferred contract workflow.

A few clarifying questions that will speed approvals:
1) Do you expect the majority of consumption to be short bursts (chat/generation) or long-running fine-tuning/embeddings? The SKU mix changes conversion math.
2) How many startups do you expect to convert to a paid plan within 60 days (rough estimate)?
3) Will BridgeFunding be the contracting party (i.e., do we invoice BridgeFunding for the accelerator top-up) or should we prepare for individual startup contracts?

If you’re open to it, Ben and I can propose a simple conditional exception: one-time top-up for the cohort + option to convert up to 50% of that top-up into a reserved commitment at an agreed discount within 60 days. I’ll let Ben sketch numbers; Laura can confirm accounting implications.

If you can confirm the three items above and re-send the small SOW page with per-company seat counts, we’ll aim to respond with a formal proposal by EOD.

—Mateo
Growth Partnerships, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com

Thanks for the loop, Mateo. I reviewed the SOW and the projected 3-month consumption profile in usage_projection.xlsx. Proposed exception framework (high level):

- Offer: Accelerator cohort one-time top-up = $30,000 in promo credits (usable across cohort startups).
- Conversion option: Up to 50% of unused top-up can be converted into a 12-month reserved commit for an individual startup if they elect to convert within 60 days of first invoice. Conversion would be at a 10% committed discount to our list reserved rates.
- Constraints: Applies only to startups accepted into BridgeFunding Labs (we need a participant roster), non-transferrable outside the cohort, and limited to one conversion event per startup.
- Accounting/billing: We invoice BridgeFunding for the top-up up-front as a promotional/invoice line item; any conversion triggers a reserved commit addendum and pro-rated credit application. Laura — can finance accept promo invoicing in this structure (promo top-up invoiced, then credit applied if conversion happens)?

Rationale: keeps contract surface area low (invoice to BridgeFunding), gives startups runway, and protects Redwood from open-ended credit leakage. If Laura signs off, I’ll draft the SOW addendum and a templated conversion addendum (DocuSign). Also recommend a short eligibility attestation the accelerator provides for each startup (simple Google Form link).

—Ben
Director, Partnerships Ops
ben_carter@redwood.com

Ben/Mateo — finance can approve the proposed structure with the following conditions:

1) We invoice BridgeFunding Labs for the $30,000 top-up net 30, and classify the line as a promotional allowance (memo on invoice required).
2) If a startup elects conversion, we will apply up to 50% of remaining top-up as a credit against a reserved capacity invoice; the conversion must be executed via a signed addendum and purchase order from either the startup or BridgeFunding (explicitly named).
3) Tax/treatment: promos applied as credit will be documented; BridgeFunding must confirm whether they require an agency-style agreement or if purchases pass-through to startups for their books. We will not convert credits to cash refunds.
4) Legal: require a short eligibility attestation list (roster + confirmation of cohort acceptance) and that BridgeFunding acknowledges the non-transferability.

Next steps: Mateo — if you can send the SOW addendum and a draft conversion addendum, I’ll review and prepare the invoice template. Ethan (cc’d finance alias) — Laura needs a signed attestation and the final participant roster before we issue the invoice.

Thanks,
